newsitem.title: USA: N.J. has bond insurance for entire $2.75 bln deal.
newsitem.headline: N.J. has bond insurance for entire $2.75 bln deal.

text.p: New Jersey has secured bids from bond insurance companies willing to insure all $2.75 billion of the state's planned pension bond deal next week, state Treasurer Brian Clymer said Friday.
"This commitment by municipal bond insurers is unprecedented in the financial markets," Clymer said in a statement. "The issuance is the largest municipal bond financing that has ever been insured."

As a result of the insurance guarantees, the bonds will carry AAA ratings from the major rating agencies. The higher ratings will save the state $69 million in gross debt service on the bonds, Clymer said.

New Jersey's largest-ever pension bond sale is part of Gov. Christine Whitman's plan to eliminate the state's unfunded pension liability. At the same time, it frees up about $590 million of budget savings for fiscal 1998.
Merrill Lynch & Co is the senior manager for the deal, and said it plans to price the issue on Wednesday. A retail order period is set to begin on Monday.
